formula: `No-show` ~ Gender + Age + Scholarship + Hipertension + Diabetes + Alcoholism + Handcap + SMS_received + (1 | PatientId) + (1 | Neighbourhood)
notes: Medical Appointment No Shows (Kaggle joniarroba/noshowappointments, Hoppen, Aquarela Analytics): medical appointments in Vitoria, Brazil, 2016, No-show Yes where the patient missed it; patients (PatientId) book several appointments and Neighbourhood is where the appointment takes place. Hand check #162: Neighbourhood, Vitória's 81 neighbourhoods (median 851 appointments, No-show varying within 79), stays a grouping factor, an area factor with many levels, against the reply's reading of exhaustive areas as design factors; 24,379 of 62,299 patients book several appointments.

RESPONSE INFERRED: Turkiye Student Evaluation (Gunduz & Fokoue, UCI 262): end-of-course evaluations by students of Gazi University, Ankara, in 13 courses (class) of 3 instructors (instr), with the student's number of attempts (nb.repeat), attendance (0-4), perceived difficulty (1-5) and 28 Likert items. UCI names no target, and Data Foundry's record (turkiye_student_evaluation) finds none for prediction but notes the grouping by instructor and course. Perceived difficulty with a random intercept per course is the reader's proposal; the instructor is a three-level covariate, and Q1 to Q28 are the other answers of the same form. Hand check #162: stands; no model of difficulty is documented.

Hand check #162: stands; each of the 22 datasets holds the 24 algorithms' errors.

formula: Score ~ Season + Age + Pos1 + Conference + Role + G + GS + MP + PTS + TRB + AST + STL + BLK + TOV + mean_views + (1 | Player_ID) + (1 | Tm)
notes: NBA players 2016-2019 (Kaggle davra98/nba-players-20162019, a university project in Milan): one row per player and season, Score the All-Star score, the ranks of the fan, player and media votes weighted 0.5, 0.25 and 0.25. Data Foundry's record (nba_players_2016_2019) groups by player, who appears in up to three seasons, and found that in 2017-18 and 2018-19 Score gives players without player or media votes the ballot size plus one as rank. No mixed model is published; random intercepts per player and team (Tm) on season-long statistics are the reader's proposal. Rk is basketball-reference's row number, Player.x the name, the vote counts and ranks build Score, and Play is the All-Star selection. Hand check #162: Tm, the league's 30 teams (median 47 player-seasons, Score varying within all), stays a grouping factor, an exhaustive set of many units, against the reply's reading as a design factor; 453 of 660 players repeat across seasons.

formula: pov ~ age + black + mother + spouse + school + hours + year_2 + year_3 + year_4 + year_5 + (1 | id)
notes: poverty.csv.gz sits in data/ at ed7b764 (first commit), but data/README.md, the paper and run_experiments.R never name it, and no ETL script writes it. It is the NLSY teenage-poverty panel of Allison's fixed-effects examples, as Williams's handout Panel Data 4 loads it (teenpovxt.dta): 1151 girls (id) in 5 yearly waves (year_2-year_5 dummies), pov in poverty, mother, spouse, school, hours worked, age and black at baseline. id the clustering unit (5 rows each). Hand check #162: Williams (Panel Data 4, pp. 3-4) fits pov on these terms with a random intercept per girl (xtlogit, re, and melogit || id:), and teenpovxt.dta equals this table in every cell, year as its dummies, so the model is published.

formula: y ~ L + K + pop + edu + (1 | group) + (1 | cl)
notes: GPBoost examples/European_GDP_spatial_grouped_data.Rmd at 981e4e4 (Sigrist, GPBoost 1.2.1): 242 NUTS2 regions in 2000 and 2021, y (log) GDP per capita, predictors L, K, pop, edu, Long and Lat the region centroid, group the region id, cl "the cluster the region belongs (there are two clusters)". Section "Other spatial random effects models": "Another option is to use a grouped random effects model defined by the categorical region ID variable", GPModel(group_data = data[, c("group", "cl")], likelihood = "gaussian") with the tree ensemble over L, K, pop, edu (chunk not evaluated); the linear fixed part is this row's rendering. Each region is observed twice. Hand check #162: the example states the grouped model on group and cl only in a chunk it does not run, with a tree-boosted mean; its one linear fit is model 1's, so this linear mean is the reader's proposal.
